audit.title: CCIP Best Practices (SVM)
audit.summary: This is a well-structured best-practices guide for building CCIP applications on Solana/SVM, with clean hierarchy (26 headings, no level skips) and several strong answer-first section leads. Its biggest strength is quotable canonical guidance ("you **must** set `allowOutOfOrderExecution` to `true`"; the token-lock caution). Its biggest opportunity is retrieval discoverability: zero JSON-LD/canonical metadata, no comparison table for the `extra_args` variants, and concept-titled headings that miss the symptom-phrased queries developers actually type ("why are my SVM tokens locked", "invalid caller ccip_receive"). Solid Good-band page with clear, surgical upside.

recommendations.title: Add an `extra_args` comparison/reference table
recommendations.where: `### Parameter Selection` and the four `Setting …` subsections
recommendations.issue: All parameter guidance is prose/bullets; "0 table(s)" in measured facts.
recommendations.change: Add a table with columns Field | Type | Applies to | Required value | Notes, rows for `compute_units`, `accountIsWritableBitmap`, `tokenReceiver`, `allowOutOfOrderExecution` (e.g. row `allowOutOfOrderExecution | bool | SVM | must be true | required source & dest`).
recommendations.why: Engines extract *reasons* and constraints from tables far more reliably than from scattered bullets; makes the SVM-specific rules liftable in one chunk.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/error-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: near `Setting tokenReceiver` and `Verify authority and allowed offramp`
recommendations.issue: Headings are concept-titled ("Verify authority and allowed offramp"); devs search "InvalidCaller ccip_receive" or "SVM tokens permanently locked".
recommendations.change: Add H3s such as "Why are my transferred tokens permanently locked?" and "Fixing `InvalidCaller` when the offramp calls `ccip_receive`", each opening with the one-sentence fix already in the body.
recommendations.why: Symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles lose, even when the answer is already present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD, canonical URL, and machine-readable dateModified
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, `programmingLanguage: [Rust, JavaScript]`, and a canonical link; surface the last-updated date in structured metadata, not just body text.
recommendations.why: Structured freshness and canonical signals raise agent trust and parse reliability. (Note: head metadata could not be verified from the served content — confirm via raw `<head>`.)

recommendations.title: Lead SVM-critical rules with the canonical requirement, answer-first
recommendations.issue: The mandatory rule sits below neutral definition prose ("controls message ordering guarantees").
recommendations.change: Open the section with the hard rule: "On SVM chains you **must** set `allowOutOfOrderExecution` to `true` (source and destination)." Keep the existing "Do NOT use an Associated Token Account (ATA)" as an explicit Don't at the top of the wallet case.
recommendations.why: Models default to the generic EVM idiom (ordered execution, ATA usage) when skimming; putting the SVM-specific canonical fact in the first liftable sentence defends against that prior.

recommendations.title: Make the Rust snippet self-contained
recommendations.issue: Measured facts flag identifiers "never assigned: EXTERNAL_EXECUTION_CONFIG_SEED, ALLOWED_OFFRAMP, STATE_SEED"; no imports.
recommendations.change: Add `use anchor_lang::prelude::*;`, the seed `const` declarations, and a one-line `Any2SVMMessage` / `CcipReceiverError` reference or link, or a comment pointing to the crate that defines them.
recommendations.why: Complete, compilable snippets are cited and reused by coding agents; undefined constants block copy-paste execution.

recommendations.title: Fill in the thin verification sections with a code or concrete check
recommendations.issue: Both are prose-only ("verify the source chain of the incoming CCIP message") with no how-to.
recommendations.change: Add a short snippet or the exact field to compare (e.g. `message.source_chain_selector` against an allowlist), mirroring the JS example in `Verify destination chain`.
recommendations.why: Concrete, symmetric examples make each section a standalone retrievable unit.

recommendations.title: Link to primary sources
recommendations.where: first mention of PDAs and Anchor accounts
recommendations.issue: "0 to primary sources" in measured facts.
recommendations.change: Add inline links to the Solana PDA documentation and Anchor `#[derive(Accounts)]` reference.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative citations raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: Placeholder comments in the Rust block (`// Additional accounts as needed // ...`) leave the example non-compilable.
Thin, prose-only sections (`Verify source chain`, `Verify sender`, `Evaluate the security…`) risk being low-value chunks.
Minor marketing-adjacent phrasing in the intro NOTE ("Our dedicated team is ready to support your projects") — harmless but not liftable content.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical, and og/twitter tags are largely site-template concerns — fix once at the layout level to benefit all CCIP pages.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good; ensure this SVM page is enumerated there.
Freshness cadence: body shows "Last Updated: 2025-05-19"; surface this as machine-readable `dateModified` site-wide.
